evidence: Routes 5 (subscale blocks) + 3 (published totals) + 7 (marker items) + an author-named-item check + direction, re-runnable as verify_CV_OASIS_ODSIS_PPE_Novak_2020_PANAS.R (server-side Redivis aggregates for the live table; OSF ex.dataset.csv only for cross-instrument checks, after proving it equals the live table: 1458 rows, max per-item mean diff 4e-15). (a) Blocks: mean r with own block vs other block, e.g. panas_2 .495/.121, panas_9 .485/.123, panas_19 .509/.124; 19/20 items closer to own block; the one exception panas_12 (alert) .332/.430, which the authors' Rmd line 1966 itself singles out ('primary: Alert') as linked to negative emotionality. The P set is the Rmd's own scoring set = canonical PA positions (1 of 184,756 10/10 splits). (b) Totals with the Rmd's actual (defective, 14-column) PANAS_P selection: live 28.92 (SD 9.89) vs published 28.83 (9.77); PANAS_N live 18.33 (7.65) vs 18.27 (7.58); r(P,N) live 0.64 Pearson vs published 0.61 Spearman. (c) Author-named items: among P items the three highest Spearman r with the OASIS total are panas_12 .298, panas_1 .126, panas_17 .098 (next panas_3 .085) = alert, interested, attentive, exactly the trio the Rmd comment names, with alert first ('primary'). (d) Markers: four lowest means are panas_13 1.367, panas_6 1.403, panas_8 1.438, panas_7 1.641 (ashamed, guilty, hostile, scared; next 1.955), all N-block. (e) Direction: r(P total, scored RSES) +0.126, r(N total, scored BFI-N) +0.447. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: order within {panas_1, panas_17}, within {6,7,8,13}, within the other six N items {2,4,11,15,18,20}, or within the other seven P items {3,5,9,10,14,16,19} -- no per-item statistics are published. It pins subscale membership, panas_12 and response direction. Hence PARTIAL.

route: explicit code labels (study codebook) + 2 range structure + published final-item list + 1 per-type published stats
evidence: Primary route: explicit code labels -- the study's codebook PDF prints each variable name (Mea1..Prod6) beside its own stem and coded options, and data/EWAS_Sanford_2024.R keeps those names (lowercased), so each of the 30 codes is tied to its text by name, not by order. Corroborated against data by verify_EWAS_Sanford_2024.R: (A) range signature 30/30 -- shipped max resp = live max resp for every item (all 5 x3 items 1..7, all 5 x5 items 1..5, the 20 others 1..6; live min 1 everywhere). (B) the 6 codes whose shipped item_text equals the 6 final-scale stems printed in paper Table 2 (prod1, enri2, enga3, sat1, mea2, enri3) are exactly the 6 live items with n = 718 (= 236 Study 1 + 482 Study 2); all other items n = 236. (C) Study 2 .sav variable labels = shipped item_text 6/6 and value labels = shipped option_text 6/6. (D) paper Table 1 average item partial r by format type, published .29/.27/.27/.25/.16/.19 vs reproduced from the Study 1 .sav grouped by the codebook's suffix->type assignment .28/.26/.27/.25/.16/.19 (max dev 0.006). What the statistics alone do NOT establish: within one domain, formats 1, 2 and 4 are not separated by A or D (e.g. sat2 vs sat4); for the 24 Study-1-only items that separation rests on the codebook's explicit name-to-text labels, which C shows are accurate wherever a data-level label exists. Status VERIFIED on the label-match route; orchestrator may downgrade to PARTIAL if a statistical separation of every item is required.
